subject: computer_science
topicTitle: Exception and File Handling in Python, Database Concepts, Structured Query Language (SQL), Computer Networks

cuetRelevance.pyqFrequency: Dominates Section A (mandatory common section). Averages 12-15 questions per paper.

summary30Seconds: Python exceptions are handled via try-except-else-finally blocks; 'finally' executes unconditionally even after return.
File handling: text files use open(filename, mode, encoding); binary files require pickle.dump(obj, f) and pickle.load(f); relative seeks like f.seek(offset, 1) require binary mode.
RDBMS terms: Relation = Table, Tuple = Row, Attribute = Column, Cardinality = Number of rows, Degree = Number of columns.
SQL commands: DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP - auto-committed), DML (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), aggregate functions ignore NULLs except COUNT(*).
Networks: Star topology uses central switch/hub; Bus uses terminator; OSI has 7 layers, TCP/IP has 4; IPv4 is 32-bit (4 bytes), IPv6 is 128-bit (16 bytes).

coreConcepts.title: 1. Python Exception Handling Architecture
coreConcepts.content: An exception is an abnormal condition or run-time error that alters the normal flow of program execution. In Python, code prone to exceptions is enclosed in a 'try' block. If an exception occurs, Python matches it against 'except' clauses sequentially. The 'else' block executes ONLY if no exception is raised in the try block. The 'finally' block is the cleanup block and is GUARANTEED to execute, regardless of whether an exception occurred, was handled, or even if a return statement was encountered inside try or except.
ncertPointers: Built-in exception hierarchy: BaseException -> Exception -> (ArithmeticError -> ZeroDivisionError, OverflowError), LookupError -> (IndexError, KeyError), ValueError, TypeError, IOError/FileNotFoundError.
The 'raise' statement explicitly triggers an exception: raise ValueError('Invalid score').
The 'assert' statement tests a condition; raises AssertionError if the condition evaluates to False.

coreConcepts.title: 2. Python File Handling (Text, Binary, and CSV)
coreConcepts.content: Files provide persistent secondary storage. Modes: 'r' (read, file must exist), 'w' (write, overwrites existing file or creates new), 'a' (append, writes at end), '+' (updates: r+, w+, a+). For binary files, append 'b' ('rb', 'wb', 'ab+'). File pointer operations: f.tell() returns current byte position; f.seek(offset, whence) repositions pointer where whence=0 (beginning, default), whence=1 (current position, binary mode only), whence=2 (end of file, binary mode only). Binary files use module 'pickle': pickle.dump(object, file_handle) for serialization and pickle.load(file_handle) for deserialization (raises EOFError at end). CSV files use module 'csv': csv.writer(file_handle, delimiter=',') with writerow() or writerows(), and csv.reader(file_handle).
ncertPointers: f.read(n) reads at most n characters/bytes; f.readline() reads a single line including '\n'; f.readlines() returns a list of lines.
The 'with open(...) as f:' context manager automatically closes the file even if exceptions occur.
When writing CSV files on Windows, open with 'newline=""' to prevent extraneous blank lines.

coreConcepts.title: 3. Relational Database Concepts & SQL Operations
coreConcepts.content:
A relational database organizes data into two-dimensional tables (relations). Key concepts: Candidate Key (minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies a tuple), Primary Key (the selected candidate key, cannot contain NULL), Alternate Key (candidate keys not chosen as primary), Foreign Key (attribute in referencing table matching the primary key of referenced table, enforces Referential Integrity). Keys ensure Entity Integrity and Domain Integrity.

SQL is divided into:
1. DDL (Data Definition): CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE (ADD, MODIFY, DROP column), DROP TABLE.
2. DML (Data Manipulation): INSERT INTO, UPDATE tablename SET col=val WHERE ..., DELETE FROM tablename WHERE ...
3. DQL (Data Query): SELECT col FROM tab WHERE ... GROUP BY col HAVING condition ORDER BY col ASC/DESC.
4. DCL/TCL: COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT.
ncertPointers: Degree = total number of attributes (columns); Cardinality = total number of tuples (rows).
Cartesian Product (Degree = D1 + D2, Cardinality = C1 * C2).
WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY.
NULL comparisons must use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL, never '= NULL'.

coreConcepts.title: 4. Computer Networks, Protocols and Topologies
coreConcepts.content: Network types: PAN (Bluetooth, <10m), LAN (within building/campus, <1km), MAN (city-wide), WAN (global/Internet). Topologies: Star (all nodes connect to central hub/switch; single node failure does not affect network; hub failure disables all), Bus (single backbone cable with terminators at both ends; minimal cabling but difficult fault isolation), Ring (tokens pass in single loop), Mesh (every node connected to every other node; highly fault-tolerant; n(n-1)/2 links for n nodes). Transmission media: Guided (Twisted pair - UTP/STP, Coaxial, Optical Fibre - uses total internal reflection, highest bandwidth, immune to EMI) and Unguided (Radio waves - omnidirectional, Micro waves - line of sight, Infrared - line of sight, cannot penetrate walls). Switching techniques: Circuit Switching vs Packet Switching.
ncertPointers: Network devices: Modem (Modulation/Demodulation), Hub (broadcast/physical layer, dumb), Switch (unicast/packet forwarding based on MAC address, data link layer), Router (routes packets based on IP address, network layer), Gateway (connects dissimilar network architectures).

Protocols: HTTP (port 80), HTTPS (port 443, SSL/TLS encrypted), FTP (port 20/21), SMTP (port 25, sending mail), POP3 (port 110, downloading mail), IMAP (port 143, syncing mail across clients), DNS (resolves domain name to IP).
IPv4 is 32 bits (4 octets, e.g. 192.168.1.1); IPv6 is 128 bits (8 groups of 4 hexadecimal digits).

workedExamples.question:
Consider the following Python code snippet:

def check_val(x):
    try:
        res = 100 / x
        return res
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        return -1
    finally:
        return 999

print(check_val(0), check_val(25))

What is the exact output of this program in CUET format?
solutionSteps: Step 1: In Python, the 'finally' clause is always executed prior to leaving the try/except statement.

Step 2: If a 'finally' clause includes a return statement, the returned value is determined by the 'finally' clause's return statement, completely discarding any return statement executed in the 'try' or 'except' blocks.
Step 3: When check_val(0) is called, ZeroDivisionError occurs, except block evaluates 'return -1', but finally block executes 'return 999', returning 999.
Step 4: When check_val(25) is called, try block calculates 100/25 = 4.0, but finally block executes 'return 999', returning 999.
workedExamples.cuetTip: CUET loves testing whether 'finally' executes when a return statement is present. The finally block ALWAYS executes, and a return inside finally overrides all earlier returns!

workedExamples.question: Table 'STUDENT' has 5 attributes and 30 tuples. Table 'ENROLLMENT' has 3 attributes and 20 tuples. What will be the Degree and Cardinality of the Cartesian Product (STUDENT × ENROLLMENT)?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Degree of a table is the total number of columns (attributes). In a Cartesian Product of relations R1 and R2, Degree = Degree(R1) + Degree(R2).
Step 3: Cardinality of a table is the total number of rows (tuples). In a Cartesian Product, Cardinality = Cardinality(R1) × Cardinality(R2).
workedExamples.cuetTip: Remember: Degree ADDS (D1 + D2), Cardinality MULTIPLIES (C1 × C2). Don't mix up columns and rows!

workedExamples.question: Which of the following SQL statements correctly lists the department names and total salary of departments having more than 5 employees, ordered by total salary descending?

options.text: SELECT Dept, SUM(Salary) FROM Emp WHERE COUNT(*) > 5 GROUP BY Dept ORDER BY SUM(Salary) DESC;
SELECT Dept, SUM(Salary) FROM Emp GROUP BY Dept HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY SUM(Salary) DESC;
SELECT Dept, SUM(Salary) FROM Emp HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 GROUP BY Dept ORDER BY 2 ASC;
SELECT Dept, TOTAL(Salary) FROM Emp GROUP BY Dept WHERE COUNT(*) > 5;

solutionSteps: Step 1: Filter conditions on aggregated groups (like COUNT(*) > 5) must be written in the HAVING clause, never in the WHERE clause.
Step 2: The correct clause order in SQL is SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY.
Step 3: In Option A, WHERE COUNT(*) > 5 is an invalid SQL syntax because aggregate functions cannot appear in WHERE.
Step 4: Option B correctly uses GROUP BY Dept followed by HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 and ORDER BY SUM(Salary) DESC.
workedExamples.cuetTip: WHERE cannot take aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, COUNT, MIN, MAX). Use HAVING to filter groups!

howCuetAsksThis.typicalStem: Which clause in Python file handling ensures the file object is closed automatically even if an exception is raised?
howCuetAsksThis.strategy: Recognize the 'with' statement (context manager) as the standard Pythonic idiom.

howCuetAsksThis.typicalStem: Match Network Devices (Hub, Switch, Router, Gateway) with their primary OSI/Function layer.
howCuetAsksThis.strategy: Hub = Physical (broadcasts), Switch = Data Link (uses MAC), Router = Network (uses IP), Gateway = Connects heterogeneous networks.

howCuetAsksThis.typicalStem:
Assertion (A): The primary key of a relational table can never contain a NULL value.
Reason (R): The Entity Integrity Constraint requires every tuple to have a unique and identifiable identity.
howCuetAsksThis.strategy: Verify both statements independently. R is the formal definition of Entity Integrity, so A and R are true and R explains A.

commonTraps.misconception: Believing 'finally' will not execute if an 'except' block has an unhandled error or a return statement.
commonTraps.whyWrong: Python guarantees execution of the 'finally' block before exiting the enclosing scope under all circumstances (except os._exit()).
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: The 'finally' block always executes for mandatory cleanup (closing files, releasing locks).
commonTraps.trapOptionExample: Option stating that the function returns immediately without executing finally.

commonTraps.misconception: Using '= NULL' in SQL to search for missing values.
commonTraps.whyWrong: In SQL, NULL represents an unknown value, so any equality test 'val = NULL' evaluates to UNKNOWN (effectively False in WHERE).
commonTraps.correctUnderstanding: Always use 'IS NULL' or 'IS NOT NULL'.
commonTraps.trapOptionExample: SELECT * FROM Emp WHERE Comm = NULL;

commonTraps.whyWrong: Students often swap Degree for rows and Cardinality for columns.
commonTraps.trapOptionExample: Stating that a table with 4 columns and 10 rows has a degree of 10.

practiceQuestions.question: Which built-in Python exception is raised when a local or global variable name is not recognized or defined?
practiceQuestions.explanation: NameError is raised when trying to access or evaluate a variable or function identifier that has not been defined in the current local or global scope.

practiceQuestions.question:
What will be the output of the following Python file pointer operation if 'sample.txt' contains the string 'COMPUTER' and is opened in text read mode?

f = open('sample.txt', 'r')
f.read(3)
pos = f.tell()
print(pos)
practiceQuestions.explanation: f.read(3) reads the first 3 characters ('COM') moving the internal file pointer to index 3. f.tell() returns the current position, which is 3.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following functions in the 'pickle' module writes an object hierarchy to an open binary file?
practiceQuestions.explanation: pickle.dump(object, file) serializes the Python object hierarchy and writes it to the specified binary file handle. pickle.load(file) reads it back.

practiceQuestions.question: Given a relational table 'TEACHER' with 6 columns and 45 rows, a user drops 2 columns and inserts 5 new rows. What are the new Degree and Cardinality of the table?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Degree is the number of columns: 6 - 2 = 4. Cardinality is the number of rows: 45 + 5 = 50.

practiceQuestions.question: Which SQL command is used to add a new column 'DateOfBirth DATE' to an already existing table 'STUDENTS'?

options.text: UPDATE TABLE STUDENTS ADD DateOfBirth DATE;
ALTER TABLE STUDENTS ADD DateOfBirth DATE;
MODIFY TABLE STUDENTS ADD DateOfBirth DATE;

practiceQuestions.explanation: ALTER TABLE <table_name> ADD <column_name> <data_type>; is the standard DDL command to append a new attribute to an existing table schema.

practiceQuestions.question: What does COUNT(Commission) return in SQL if a table has 10 rows and 3 of them have NULL in the Commission column?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Aggregate functions in SQL like COUNT(column_name), SUM, and AVG ignore NULL values. Therefore, COUNT(Commission) counts only non-null entries: 10 - 3 = 7. Note that COUNT(*) would return 10.

practiceQuestions.question: Which network device operates at the Data Link Layer (Layer 2) of the OSI model and forwards incoming frames based on physical hardware MAC addresses?
practiceQuestions.explanation: A Switch operates at Layer 2 (Data Link Layer) and forwards data frames selectively to destination ports by learning and inspecting hardware MAC addresses.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): Optical fibre cables provide significantly higher transmission bandwidth and immunity to electromagnetic interference compared to copper cables.
Reason (R): Optical fibre transmits data as light pulses through a core using the physical phenomenon of Total Internal Reflection (TIR).

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and transmitting light pulses via Total Internal Reflection eliminates electrical crosstalk and electromagnetic interference, allowing ultra-high bandwidth.

Assertion (A): The 'else' block associated with a 'try-except' construct in Python executes only when an exception is raised and successfully handled.
Reason (R): The 'finally' block executes unconditionally regardless of whether an exception occurred or was handled.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match the Network Protocols in List I with their Primary Purpose in List II:
List I:
(P) SMTP
(Q) DNS
(R) POP3
(S) HTTP

List II:
(1) Resolving host names to IP addresses
(2) Sending outgoing email messages
(3) Transferring hypertext web pages
(4) Downloading emails from mail server to client
practiceQuestions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends emails (P-2); DNS translates domain names to IPs (Q-1); POP3 retrieves emails onto a local client (R-4); HTTP transfers hypermedia documents (S-3). Matches option A.
